nodes.title: Note values: whole to sixteenth
nodes.whyImportant: Every rhythm is built from these lengths, each half the one before.

nodes.title: Rest values
nodes.whyImportant: Silence is measured as exactly as sound, and every note value has a rest of the same length.

nodes.title: Dotted notes
nodes.whyImportant: A dot adds half the note's value again, which makes the long-short rhythms in most melodies.

nodes.title: Double-dotted notes
nodes.whyImportant: A second dot adds half the first dot again, and it turns up in slow movements and Grade 5 theory.

nodes.title: Ties
nodes.whyImportant: A tie joins two notes of the same pitch into one longer sound, so a note can last across a beat or a barline.

nodes.title: Ties versus slurs
nodes.whyImportant: Both are curved lines, but a tie lengthens one note and a slur shapes several, so misreading one changes the rhythm.

nodes.title: Beats and their divisions

nodes.whyImportant: Saying "1 e & a" out loud ties every note to a place in the beat, which is how rhythms are learned and checked.

nodes.title: Beat units: the bottom number

items.prompt: How many eighth notes (quavers) last as long as one half note (minim)?

answer.explanation: A half note is two quarter notes, and each quarter note is two eighth notes.

wrong.explanation: Two quarter notes make a half note; eighth notes are half as long as quarters, so it takes four.
Eight eighth notes fill a whole note, which is twice as long as a half note.

items.prompt: Which single note lasts as long as two quarter notes?

answer.explanation: Each value is twice the one below it, so a half note equals two quarter notes.

wrong.explanation: A whole note lasts four quarter notes, twice as long as asked.
An eighth note is half of one quarter note, not two of them.

items.prompt: How many flags does a single sixteenth note (semiquaver) have?

answer.explanation: Each flag halves the value: one flag is an eighth note, two flags a sixteenth.

wrong.explanation: One flag makes an eighth note, twice as long as a sixteenth.
Three flags make a thirty-second note, half as long as a sixteenth.

items.prompt: A whole rest and a half rest are both small blocks. How do you tell them apart on the staff?

answer.text: The whole rest hangs below the fourth line; the half rest sits on the middle line
answer.explanation: Their shape is the same, so their place on the staff is what tells them apart.

wrong.text: The whole rest is drawn twice as big
wrong.explanation: They are drawn the same size; only their position differs.

wrong.text: The half rest has a flag
wrong.explanation: Flags belong to the eighth rest and shorter rests, not to the half rest.

items.prompt: How many beats of silence does a quarter rest give in 4/4?

answer.explanation: A quarter rest lasts as long as a quarter note, which is one beat in 4/4.

wrong.explanation: Half a beat of silence in 4/4 is an eighth rest.
Two beats of silence in 4/4 is a half rest.

items.prompt: In 4/4, how many beats does a dotted half note last?

answer.explanation: A half note is two beats and the dot adds half of that, one more beat.

wrong.explanation: Two beats is an undotted half note; the dot adds one more.
Four beats is a whole note; the dot adds half of two beats, not two whole beats.

items.prompt: A dotted quarter note lasts as long as which tied pair?

answer.text: A quarter note tied to an eighth note
answer.explanation: The dot adds half of a quarter note, which is an eighth note.

wrong.text: A quarter note tied to a quarter note
wrong.explanation: Two tied quarter notes make a half note; the dot adds only half a quarter.

wrong.text: A quarter note tied to a sixteenth note
wrong.explanation: A sixteenth is a quarter of a quarter note; the dot adds half, an eighth.

items.prompt: In 4/4, a dotted quarter note on beat 1 is followed by which note to reach beat 3?

answer.explanation: A dotted quarter is one and a half beats, and an eighth note adds the last half beat.

wrong.explanation: That makes two and a half beats, so the next note would start halfway through beat 3.
That makes one and three quarter beats, a sixteenth short of beat 3.

items.prompt: In 4/4, how many beats does a double-dotted half note last?

answer.explanation: Two beats, plus one for the first dot, plus half a beat for the second dot.

wrong.explanation: Three beats is a single-dotted half note; the second dot adds half a beat more.
The second dot adds half of the first dot, half a beat, not a whole beat.

items.prompt: What does the second dot of a double-dotted note add?

answer.text: Half the value of the first dot
answer.explanation: Each dot adds half of what the one before it added.

wrong.text: The same as the first dot
wrong.explanation: If it did, a double-dotted half note would last four beats instead of three and a half.

wrong.text: Half the value of the note itself
wrong.explanation: That is what the first dot adds; the second adds half of that again.

items.prompt: Two quarter notes on the same pitch are joined by a curved line. How do you play them?

answer.text: Play once and hold for two beats
answer.explanation: A tie adds the second value to the first: one attack, two beats long.

wrong.explanation: Playing twice smoothly is what a slur asks of different pitches; a tie is never struck again.

wrong.text: Play twice, the second one louder
wrong.explanation: A tie gives the second note no attack at all.

items.prompt: Why write a half note tied over the barline to a quarter note, instead of a dotted half note?

answer.text: A note cannot cross a barline, so a tie carries it into the next bar
answer.explanation: Each bar must add up on its own; the tie lets a sound continue past the barline.

wrong.text: The tie makes the note louder
wrong.explanation: A tie changes only the length of a note, never its volume.

wrong.text: The tied notes are shorter than a dotted half
wrong.explanation: Both last three beats; the difference is only where the barline falls.

items.prompt: A curved line joins a C to the D after it. What is it?

answer.text: A slur: play both, smoothly connected
answer.explanation: A curve between different pitches is a slur; both notes are played.

wrong.text: A tie: hold the C through the D
wrong.explanation: A tie only ever joins two notes of the same pitch.

wrong.text: A pause over the two notes
wrong.explanation: A pause is a curve with a dot above one note, not a line joining two notes.

items.prompt: A curved line joins two notes of the same pitch, side by side. How many times do you strike the key?

answer.explanation: Same pitch, adjacent, joined by a curve: that is a tie, so you strike once and hold for both values.

wrong.explanation: Striking twice is what you would do with no curve at all or with a slur over different notes.

wrong.text: Not at all; it is a rest
wrong.explanation: A tie joins sounding notes; silence is written with rests.

items.prompt: In simple time, each beat divides into how many equal parts?

answer.explanation: Simple time splits the beat in two, as a quarter note splits into two eighths.

wrong.explanation: A beat that divides into three is compound time, like 6/8.
No standard metre divides its beat into five; five notes in a beat is a special grouping.

items.prompt: In 2/4, how many eighth notes fill one beat?

answer.explanation: The beat in 2/4 is a quarter note, which divides into two eighth notes.

wrong.explanation: One eighth note is only half of a quarter-note beat.
Four eighth notes fill a whole bar of 2/4, which has two beats.

items.prompt: Counting sixteenth notes as "1 e & a", which syllable falls exactly halfway through the beat?

answer.explanation: The "&" splits the beat in half; "e" and "a" mark the quarters either side of it.

wrong.explanation: "e" comes a quarter of the way through the beat, the second sixteenth.
"a" comes three quarters of the way through the beat, the last sixteenth.

items.prompt: Counting 4/4 as "1 & 2 & 3 & 4 &", where does a note on the "&" of 2 begin?

answer.explanation: The "&" is the second half of the beat it follows.

wrong.explanation: A note on beat 2 is counted "2"; the "&" comes half a beat later.
A note on beat 3 is counted "3"; the "&" of 2 comes half a beat earlier.

items.prompt: In 2/2 (cut time), which note gets the beat?

answer.explanation: The bottom 2 means a half note, so the bar has two half-note beats.

wrong.explanation: A quarter-note beat is written with a 4 at the bottom, as in 2/4.
A whole note is the whole bar of 2/2, not one beat of it.

items.prompt: Which time signature does the symbol C stand for?

answer.explanation: C is common time, four quarter-note beats in a bar.

wrong.explanation: 2/2 is cut time, written as a C with a vertical line through it.
3/4 has no symbol of its own; it is always written as numbers.

items.prompt: What fills one bar of 3/8?

answer.explanation: The top 3 counts the beats and the bottom 8 makes each one an eighth note.

wrong.explanation: Three quarter notes fill a bar of 3/4; the 8 at the bottom means eighth notes.
A sixteenth-note beat would be written with 16 at the bottom.

items.prompt: Which kind of metre is 3/4?

answer.explanation: Three beats in a bar, each dividing into two: simple triple.

wrong.explanation: Simple duple has two beats in a bar, as in 2/4.
Compound duple has two beats that each divide into three, as in 6/8.

items.prompt: Which time signature is simple quadruple?

answer.explanation: Four beats in a bar, each dividing into two.

wrong.explanation: 2/4 has two beats in a bar: simple duple.
12/8 has four beats, but each divides into three, so it is compound quadruple.

items.prompt: At a moderate tempo, how many beats do you feel in a bar of 6/8?

answer.explanation: The six eighth notes group in two threes, and each three is one beat.

wrong.explanation: The six eighth notes are the divisions of the beat; counted one by one they are only felt at very slow tempos.
Three beats of two eighth notes is 3/4, which holds the same notes grouped differently.

items.prompt: In compound time, each beat divides into how many equal parts?

answer.explanation: A dotted beat splits evenly into three, as a dotted quarter splits into three eighths.

wrong.explanation: A beat that divides into two is simple time.
Four parts is the second division of a simple beat, as in sixteenth notes.

items.prompt: Both 6/8 and 3/4 hold six eighth notes. What is the difference?

answer.text: 6/8 has two beats of three eighths; 3/4 has three beats of two
answer.explanation: The notes are the same; how they group into beats is not.

wrong.explanation: The grouping differs, so the strong beats fall in different places.
A time signature says nothing about speed; the tempo marking does.

items.prompt: Which metre is 12/8?

answer.explanation: Twelve eighth notes in groups of three make four dotted-quarter beats.

wrong.text: Twelve beats of an eighth note
wrong.explanation: In compound time the eighth notes are divisions; they group in threes into beats.
Compound triple is 9/8, three groups of three eighth notes.

items.prompt: Which time signature is compound triple?

answer.explanation: Nine eighth notes grouped in threes give three dotted-quarter beats.

wrong.explanation: 3/4 has three beats that each divide into two: simple triple.
6/8 has two dotted-quarter beats: compound duple.

items.prompt: In 6/8, 9/8 or 12/8, what does the top number divided by three give?

answer.text: The number of beats in a bar
answer.explanation: Each beat holds three of the counted notes, so dividing by three counts the beats.

wrong.text: The note that gets the beat
wrong.explanation: The beat is a dotted note; dividing the top number tells how many, not which.
A time signature never sets the speed.

items.prompt: How is a bar of 7/8 usually grouped?

answer.text: Into unequal beats of twos and threes, such as 2+2+3
answer.explanation: Seven eighth notes cannot split into equal twos or threes, so the beats are of unequal length.

wrong.explanation: Seven does not divide evenly by three.
Groups of only threes would need six or nine eighth notes, not seven.

items.prompt: A bar of 5/8 is grouped 3+2. How many beats does it have?

answer.text: Two: one long and one short
answer.explanation: Each group is one beat, so a 3+2 bar has a long beat and then a short one.

wrong.explanation: The five eighth notes are grouped into beats; they are not each a beat.
Three is the size of the first group, not the number of groups.

items.prompt: Which fills exactly one bar of 3/4?

answer.text: A half note and a quarter note
answer.explanation: Two beats plus one beat makes the three beats of 3/4.

wrong.explanation: Two half notes make four beats, one too many for 3/4.

wrong.text: A dotted half note and a quarter note
wrong.explanation: A dotted half note already fills 3/4; the quarter note overflows the bar.

items.prompt: A bar of 4/4 holds a half note and a quarter note. What completes it?

answer.text: A quarter note or a quarter rest
answer.explanation: Two beats and one beat make three; one more beat makes four.

wrong.explanation: That makes five beats, one too many.
That makes three and a half beats, half a beat short.

items.prompt: In 4/4, how are eight eighth notes usually beamed?

answer.text: In two groups of four, beats 1-2 and 3-4
answer.explanation: Beams may join beats 1 and 2 or 3 and 4, but never beat 2 to beat 3 across the middle of the bar.

wrong.explanation: One beam hides the middle of the bar, where beat 3 starts.
Groups of three show compound beats, which 4/4 does not have.

items.prompt: In 6/8, how are six eighth notes beamed?

answer.explanation: Each group of three is one dotted-quarter beat.

wrong.explanation: Three groups of two show the three beats of 3/4, not the two beats of 6/8.

wrong.text: Each eighth note with its own flag
wrong.explanation: Separate flags hide the beats; beams are used to show them.

items.prompt: In 4/4, silence on beats 2 and 3 is written how?

answer.explanation: A half rest starting on beat 2 would hide the middle of the bar, so two quarter rests show beat 3.

wrong.explanation: In 4/4 a half rest belongs on beat 1 or beat 3, where it does not hide the middle of the bar.
A whole rest silences the entire bar, not two beats of it.

items.prompt: In 3/4, how is a whole bar of silence written?

answer.explanation: A whole rest means a whole bar of silence in any time signature.

wrong.explanation: A whole bar of rest is written with a whole rest, whatever the metre.
Three quarter rests add up correctly, but a whole bar is shown with one whole rest.

items.prompt: In 2/4, what does a 3 over three eighth notes mean?

answer.text: Play the three evenly in the time of two eighth notes, one beat
answer.explanation: A triplet squeezes three equal notes into the time two would take.

wrong.explanation: The 3 is a grouping number, not an accent.

wrong.text: Hold the group for three beats
wrong.explanation: The group lasts one beat; the 3 counts the notes in it.

items.prompt: How many eighth-note triplets fill one quarter-note beat?

answer.explanation: A triplet is three notes in the time of two eighths, which is one quarter-note beat.

wrong.explanation: Two plain eighth notes fill a beat; a triplet puts three in that space.
Six triplet eighths fill two beats, or one beat of sixteenth-note triplets.

items.prompt: In 6/8, what is a duplet?

answer.text: Two equal notes in the time of three eighth notes
answer.explanation: A duplet splits a dotted beat in two instead of three.

wrong.text: Three notes in the time of two
wrong.explanation: That is a triplet, which borrows the other way.

wrong.text: Two notes in the time of four
wrong.explanation: Two notes in the time of four is just two quarter notes; nothing is borrowed.

items.prompt: In which kind of metre do duplets usually appear?

answer.explanation: They borrow the simple division of two into a beat that normally divides into three.

wrong.explanation: A simple beat already divides into two, so there is nothing to borrow.
Duplets belong to compound metres like 6/8; 4/4 is simple.

items.prompt: What is syncopation?

answer.text: Stress that falls off the beat or on a weak beat
answer.explanation: It works by going against the expected pattern of strong and weak beats.

wrong.explanation: A change of speed is a tempo change, not syncopation.

wrong.text: Any bar that contains a rest
wrong.explanation: A rest can help make syncopation, but a rest on its own is not syncopation.

items.prompt: Which rhythm in 4/4 is syncopated?

answer.text: Eighth, quarter, eighth on beats 1 and 2
answer.explanation: The quarter note starts on the "&" of 1 and holds through beat 2, so beat 2 gets no new note.

wrong.explanation: Every note lands on a beat, so nothing goes against the pulse.
Both notes land on strong beats, 1 and 3.

items.prompt: How does a tie often create syncopation?

answer.text: It holds a note from an off-beat over the next beat
answer.explanation: The beat that follows gets no new attack, so the stress falls on the off-beat.

wrong.text: It makes the tied note louder
wrong.explanation: A tie only changes length.

wrong.text: It shortens the note to half a beat
wrong.explanation: A tie always lengthens a note.

items.prompt: A piece in 3/4 starts with one quarter note before the first full bar. What is that note called?

answer.explanation: Notes before the first full bar make an anacrusis.

wrong.explanation: Syncopation is stress against the beat; an anacrusis is just an incomplete opening bar.
The downbeat is beat 1 of the first full bar, which comes after the anacrusis.

items.prompt: A piece in 3/4 opens with a one-beat anacrusis. How long is its last bar, usually?

answer.explanation: The anacrusis and the last bar usually add up to one full bar.

wrong.explanation: The opening beat is usually taken from the last bar, so it is a beat short.
One beat at the end would add up to two beats with the anacrusis, not a full bar of 3/4.

items.prompt: Which bar is bar 1 in a piece with an anacrusis?

answer.text: The first full bar after the anacrusis
answer.explanation: The incomplete opening bar is not counted.

wrong.explanation: Bar numbers start with the first complete bar.
The first full bar is bar 1.

items.prompt: How many quarter-note beats does a breve last?

answer.explanation: A breve is two whole notes, and each whole note is four quarter notes.

wrong.explanation: Four quarter notes is a whole note; the breve is twice as long.
Six quarter notes is a dotted whole note.

items.prompt: Which note is twice as long as a whole note?

answer.explanation: Each value doubles the one below it, and the breve is the next step up from the whole note.

wrong.explanation: A dot adds half, so a dotted whole note is one and a half whole notes.
A half note is half as long as a whole note.

items.prompt: How many thirty-second notes fill one quarter note?

answer.explanation: A quarter note is four sixteenths, and each sixteenth is two thirty-seconds.

wrong.explanation: Four sixteenth notes fill a quarter note; thirty-seconds are half as long.
Sixteen thirty-second notes fill a half note.

items.prompt: How many beams join a group of thirty-second notes?

answer.explanation: One beam per flag: eighths have one, sixteenths two, thirty-seconds three.

wrong.explanation: Two beams join sixteenth notes.
Four beams join sixty-fourth notes.

items.prompt: What does "quarter note = 120" at the top of a piece mean?

answer.explanation: The number counts how many of the named note fit in a minute.

wrong.explanation: The mark counts the named note, not bars.
It sets the speed of the beat, not the length of the piece.

items.prompt: At quarter note = 60, how long does each quarter note last?

answer.explanation: Sixty beats in sixty seconds is one beat per second.

wrong.explanation: Half a second per beat is quarter note = 120.
Two seconds per beat is quarter note = 30.
